topics.topic: The Trans-Atlantic Slave Trade: Origins, triangular trade network, and abolition
learningObjectives: Trace the origins and geopolitical factors establishing the triangular trade connecting Europe, West Africa, and the Americas
Analyze the horrific Middle Passage and slave trading coastal ports in Nigeria (Badagry, Bonny, Calabar, Lagos)
Examine the economic, demographic, and moral factors spurring the British Abolition Act of 1807

topics.topic: Transition to Legitimate Commerce: Palm oil trade, groundnuts, and rise of merchant princes
learningObjectives: Define legitimate commerce as trade in agricultural and natural commodities in post-abolition 19th-century Nigeria
Explain the strategic rise of the palm oil trade in the Niger Delta to fuel Industrial Revolution machines in Britain
Analyze the rise of powerful merchant princes: King Jaja of Opobo, Nana Olomu of Itsekiri, and King William Pepple of Bonny

topics.topic: Christian Missionary Enterprises in Nigeria: CMS, Catholic, Methodist, and Presbyterian missions
learningObjectives: Trace the arrival of Christian missionaries starting in Badagry (1842) led by Thomas Birch Freeman and Henry Townsend
Evaluate the monumental scholarly and ecclesiastical contributions of Bishop Samuel Ajayi Crowther
Examine missionary impacts: introduction of Western education, printing presses, vernacular Bible translation, and stopping twin killing

topics.topic: 19th Century Yoruba Wars (Kiriji / Ekitiparapo War): Causes, course, and peacemaking (1886)
learningObjectives: Analyze the causes of 19th-century warfare following the fall of Old Oyo: Ibadan's imperialist ambitions and tribute extraction
Trace the formation of the Ekitiparapo confederacy led by Fabunmi of Imesi-Ile and Ogedengbe of Ilesa
Examine the protracted Kiriji war tactics, introduction of breech-loading rifles, and the British-mediated Peace Treaty of 1886

topics.topic: European Explorers and Geopolitical Scramble: Mungo Park, the Landers, and Berlin Conference (1884-1885)
learningObjectives: Trace British exploratory expeditions to map the course and termination of the River Niger (Mungo Park, Clapperton, Lander brothers)
Analyze the Berlin Conference (1884-1885) convened by Otto von Bismarck and the principle of 'effective occupation'
Examine how European imperial powers carved out African spheres of influence without African consent

topics.topic: The Royal Niger Company: Sir George Goldie, commercial monopoly, and treaties of cession
learningObjectives: Examine Sir George Goldie's role in amalgamating British trading firms into the National African Company (Royal Niger Company)
Analyze the 1886 Royal Charter granting the company administrative and military powers over the Niger territories
Examine dubious treaties of cession signed with local chiefs and the company’s monopoly enforcing gunboat diplomacy

topics.topic: Mid-Term Continuous Assessment & Imperial Treaties Analysis Clinic
learningObjectives: Assess pupil comprehension of the slave trade transition, missionary enterprises, and the Berlin Conference
Examine historical primary source treaties signed between the Royal Niger Company and traditional rulers
Remediate student confusion regarding the sequence of 19th-century colonial treaties

topics.topic: British Military Conquest and Indigenous Resistance: Lagos Annexation (1861) and Jaja of Opobo
learningObjectives: Analyze the British bombardment of Lagos (1851), the deposition of Oba Kosoko, and the formal 1861 Treaty of Cession by Oba Dosunmu
Examine King Jaja of Opobo’s defiance of British commercial encroachment on inland oil markets
Trace the fraudulent abduction, trial, and exile of Jaja to the West Indies by Consul Harry Johnston in 1887

topics.topic: British Conquest and Indigenous Resistance: Nana Olomu, Oba Ovonramwen of Benin (1897)
learningObjectives: Examine Nana Olomu of Itsekiri's trading stronghold at Ebrohimi and the 1894 British military siege
Analyze the 1897 British Punitive Expedition against the Kingdom of Benin following the Phillips incident
Trace the looting of thousands of sacred Benin bronzes and the deposition and exile of Oba Ovonramwen to Calabar

topics.topic: British Conquest of Northern Nigeria: Fall of Kano, Sokoto (1903), and Satiru Uprising
learningObjectives: Trace Lord Lugard’s military expeditions against the Emirates of Northern Nigeria using the West African Frontier Force (WAFF)
Analyze the resistance and fall of Kano and the battle of Sokoto leading to the martyrdom of Sultan Attahiru I at Burmi (1903)
Examine the 1906 messianic Satiru peasant rebellion and severe British reprisals

topics.topic: The 1914 Amalgamation of Nigeria: Lord Lugard, colonial administrative objectives, and immediate impacts
learningObjectives: Analyze economic and administrative rationales behind merging the Northern and Southern Protectorates in 1914
Examine Lord Frederick Lugard’s administrative architecture and the amalgamation report
Critique the structural defects and lasting fault lines created by unifying distinct sovereign nations under colonial rule

topics.topic: Comprehensive SSS 2 History Termly Revision & Historical Source Analysis
learningObjectives: Consolidate learning across 19th-century wars, missionary movements, colonial conquest, and the 1914 amalgamation
Practice timed essay writing answering past WASSCE History Paper 2 questions with historical citations
Refine student capability in evaluating bias in colonial dispatches and indigenous oral chronicles
Administer official SSS 2 History end-of-term examination
Grade theory scripts according to standardized West African Examinations Council criteria
Record and publish official continuous assessment and examination results
